biggest_catch: The $350 annual fee plus the miles having no fixed cash value. Year-one math: 60,000 miles are worth roughly $660-$720 in flights at typical valuations (about 1.1-1.2 cents per mile), plus 500 Premier Qualifying Points if you reach the spend, minus the $350 annual fee, which leaves roughly $310 net in the first year (PQP value excluded because it only matters toward elite status). Only claim this if you were already going to spend $4,000 in 3 months on normal purchases; never spend extra to hit the target. The bonus is unavailable if you currently hold the Quest or received its new-cardmember bonus in the past 24 months, and Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern applies.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $4,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: 60,000 miles are worth roughly $660-$720 in flights at typical valuations, minus the $350 annual fee, which leaves about $310 net before the travel credits and perks. The $200 inflight and United Hotels credits only have value if you actually fly United and use them. Miles are not cash and devaluation risk is real.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.
The bonus is not available if you currently have the Quest card or received a new-cardmember bonus on the Quest in the past 24 months. Check the current application terms before applying.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit.

The extra 10,000 miles require adding an authorized user who makes a purchase in the first 3 months, and the 500 PQPs require the full $4,000 spend; the account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid.

steps: Go to the official Chase United cards page, select Quest, and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm your eligibility: you do not currently hold the Quest and have not received its new-cardmember bonus in the past 24 months.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $4,000 in the first 3 months from account opening.
If you want the extra 10,000 miles, add an authorized user who makes a purchase in the first 3 months.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met for the miles and PQPs to post, and confirm they appear in your MileagePlus account.
Before the second $350 annual fee hits, check whether your real United flying and perks beat $350 a year, and downgrade or cancel if not.
timing: Spend $4,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Bonus posts after qualifying purchases, typically 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met.
